name: Gallows
overview: The biblical use of gallows, as depicted in the book of Esther, highlights their function as instruments of capital punishment for criminals and enemies of the king. The narrative vividly illustrates the gallows as a symbol of divine justice and reversal of fortune, where Haman, who plotted evil against Mordecai and the Jews, is ultimately executed on the very gallows he had prepared for Mordecai. This method of execution carried not only physical but also public reproach, emphasizing the shame associated with being hanged, as seen in the hanging of Haman and his sons. Through these accounts, the gallows serve as a sobering reminder of God's sovereignty and righteous judgment against wickedness.
